physics_goals.value: Measure or bound the branching ratio of the CP-violating rare decay KL -> pi0 nu nubar

summary.plain: KOTO is a Japanese experiment at J-PARC that watches for an extremely rare kaon decay into a neutral pion and two invisible neutrinos, testing the same physics as NA62 but with the neutral, longer-lived kind of kaon.
summary.technical: J-PARC E14 KOTO: fixed-target experiment at the J-PARC Hadron Experimental Facility measuring/bounding the branching ratio of the CP-violating decay KL -> pi0 nu nubar. First physics run May 2013 (100 hours, 24 kW beam); physics running resumed April 2015; has published results from 2015, 2016-2018, 2018 and 2021 data, most recently in February 2025; successor to the KEK-PS E391a experiment.
